ACT, 1961, NOW PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC COURT SOMAWARAPETE KODAGU DISTRICT AGAINST THE PETITIONERS VIDE ANNEXURES-A.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed by the husband and in-laws seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in C.C.No.524/2024 arising out of Crime No.97/2024 for the offence punishable under sections 498(A), 323, 506, 34 of IPC and sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
NC: 2025:KHC:39179 HC-KAR 2.
Today, when the matter was taken up, both parties were kept present before this Court for the purpose of recording the compromise.
Respondent No.2, the de facto complainant, is present before this Court.
On being specifically queried, she submits that the matter was amicably settled before the Mediation Centre, and pursuant thereto, a Memorandum of Settlement has been drawn.
The said settlement has already been placed before the Family Court in M.C.No.5202/2025 for recording dissolution of marriage.

In terms of the settlement, respondent No.2 has categorically stated that Chirag vs State Of Karnataka on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143825831/
2
she intends to withdraw all allegations made against the petitioners and she has no objection to quashing of the present proceedings.

3. Recording the submission of respondent No.2, and in view of the fact that the matrimonial dispute between the parties has been substantially resolved in the pending proceedings for dissolution of marriage, this Court is satisfied that no fruitful purpose would be served by allowing the criminal prosecution to continue.

Since the husband and wife have mutually agreed to part ways by securing a decree of NC: 2025:KHC:39179 HC-KAR divorce, continuation of the present criminal proceedings would only amount to an abuse of process of law and would cause unnecessary hardship to both sides.
4. For the foregoing reasons, this Court finds it a fit case to exercise its inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to secure the ends of justice.
ORDER i.
The criminal petition is hereby allowed.

ii. The proceedings pending in C.C.No.525/2024,
arising out of Crime No.97/2024 registered by Shanivarasanthe police station, and pending on the file of the Senior Civil Judge And Jmfc Court Somawarapete, Kodagu District for the offence punishable u/s 498A, 323, 506, 34 OF IPC AND section 3, 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, in so far as the petitioners are concerned, stand quashed.
